$comment: ONE version for the whole app, not one per package. The frontend and the
backend ship together -- `docker compose up -d --build` brings up both --
so two independently-moving versions would describe a split that does not
release-type is `simple`: it owns .release-please-manifest.json as the
source of truth and writes the version back into frontend/package.json
through extra-files. The backend has no version file of its own and does
not need one; app/name_cache.py already embeds orthonym.__version__ for
the only versioning that is load-bearing at runtime (cache invalidation).
Starting at 0.1.0 on purpose. Under semver, 0.x says breaking changes are
expected -- which is the honest reading of a product whose own census
records 109 of 544 names still fully inert and one named regression.
bump-minor-pre-major keeps a `feat:` at 0.x -> 0.(x+1).0 rather than
jumping to 1.0.0 before the coverage story is finished.
test/build/ci/chore are hidden from the changelog, not ignored: they still
bump the version, they just do not clutter release notes a user reads.
